summary: A free full text of the pollinosis RCT 35776034 was found on the publisher's site (via its DOI, after the OpenAlex lookup) and read: 66 Japanese adults with seasonal eye/nose symptoms took Quercetin Phytosome (200 mg quercetin/day) or placebo for 4 weeks; the primary JRQLQ showed lower total, QOL, sleep and physical scores with selected item improvements, without multiplicity adjustment and with Indena funding. This narrow allergy-symptom context is credited, gated to a label claim for seasonal allergy symptoms and to phytosome forms; antiviral and senolysis claims are excluded per Dr. Pham. The open-label COVID-19 trial (36712674) remains approved without credit, and 40037045 (pharmacokinetics; hybrid OA at ScienceDirect blocked by bot detection) gets no context because absorption cannot stand in for benefit.

applicability.studied_population: Adults aged 22-78 with seasonal (pollinosis) eye and nose symptoms, taking Quercetin Phytosome providing 200 mg quercetin/day for 4 weeks.

identity.standardization: Lecithin-based phytosome delivery system; 50 mg quercetin per tablet

population.description: 66 Japanese adults aged 22-78 with relatively high JRQLQ nose/eye symptom scores during pollen season (pollinosis-type eye/nose discomfort), excluding people using anti-allergy drugs; 64 in safety set (32 per arm), 60 per protocol.

study_contexts.study_design: Randomized placebo-controlled double-blind parallel-group trial, 4 weeks, at a single clinic in Tokyo; vehicle placebo tablets.

outcomes.name: Primary JRQLQ: absolute total, QOL total, sleep and physical scores lower than placebo; change from baseline significant for sleep (4W -1.0 vs -0.1) and physical scores; selected items (sneezing, malaise, sleep disorder) significant
Secondary allergic-rhinitis severity: sneezing, rhinorrhea and daily-living disturbance lower than placebo; nasal-discharge eosinophils lower at 2 weeks

limitations: No adjustment for multiple items and time points; several JRQLQ domains did not differ; paper prints significance as 'p<0.05%'. Small 4-week trial.
Funded by Indena (Indena Japan and Indena S.p.A.), with an Indena Japan co-author and Indena-supported editorial assistance.
200 mg is the quercetin content (4 x 50 mg tablets), not the whole phytosome mass; exact Quercetin Phytosome only; no transfer to plain quercetin.
Allergy-symptom (pollinosis) context only; not immune, antiviral or senolytic evidence.
Dr. Pham's returned decision A137: absorption-to-general-benefit, antiviral and senolysis transfers rejected; narrower contexts only.
Context authored and source-verified by agent review (Claude) on 2026-10-28; Dr. Pham's pre-approval of fully source-verified contexts attested by Sean on 2026-10-28.

dose.administration_frequency: Two tablets with breakfast and two with supper, with water.
co_therapies: Anti-allergy drugs, antihistamines, steroids and vasoconstrictors were not allowed during the study (exclusion criteria).
dose.reported_regimen: Four Quercetin Phytosome tablets daily (50 mg quercetin each; 200 mg quercetin/day) in two doses for 4 weeks.

normalization.basis: 4 x 50 mg = 200 mg quercetin/day as supplied in phytosome tablets; whole phytosome mass not stated.

source_provenance.location: Subjects and Methods (inclusion/exclusion criteria, test food: 50 mg quercetin per tablet, four tablets/day in two doses; primary endpoint JRQLQ; statistics); Results (flow: 66 enrolled, 64 safety, 60 per protocol; Tables II-IV); conflict of interest

identity.standardization: 500 mg Quercetin Phytosome per tablet (lecithin-based quercetin delivery)

population.description: Adults >=18 with RT-PCR-confirmed mild to moderate symptomatic COVID-19 at King Edward Medical University, Lahore; 108 randomized, 100 completed (50 per group).

study_contexts.study_design: Single-centre open-label randomized controlled trial: standard of care plus Quercetin Phytosome vs standard of care alone; 2 weeks.

outcomes.name: Primary: RT-PCR negative at day 7, 34 vs 12 patients (p=0.0004); by week 2 most participants in both arms negative
Primary: COVID-19 acute symptoms resolved by day 7, 26 vs 12 patients (p=0.0051)
LDH fell significantly; CRP, ferritin and D-dimer improvements reported

limitations: Open-label, standard-of-care control without placebo; single centre.
Not scoring eligible: antiviral transfer rejected by Dr. Pham; no infection treatment or prevention claim follows for supplements.
Returned decision A137: absorption-to-general-benefit, antiviral and senolysis transfers rejected; narrower contexts only.
Context authored and source-verified by agent review (Claude) on 2026-10-28; Dr. Pham's pre-approval of fully source-verified contexts attested by Sean on 2026-10-28.

dose.administration_frequency: One 500 mg tablet three times daily in week 1, then twice daily in week 2.
co_therapies: Standard of care for COVID-19 in both arms.
dose.reported_regimen: Quercetin Phytosome 500 mg tablet TDS week 1 (1,500 mg/day), BDS week 2 (1,000 mg/day), added to standard of care.

normalization.basis: Whole Quercetin Phytosome tablet mass per day as assigned; not converted to pure quercetin.

source_provenance.location: Abstract; Methods (design, inclusion, treatment paragraph, primary outcomes); Results (flow, PCR, symptoms, Table 2)

integration_notes: 2026-10-28 integrator: require_source_label_form removed; required_form_terms kept, matching the KSM-66/Tesnor precedent. Source-only matching rejected real labels whose ingredient row resolves through the enricher.

2026-10-28 integrator: condition gate kept (supported_outcomes ['seasonal_allergy_symptoms'] equals the context condition). Sean's decision is that a claim-free label may earn scoped condition credit, but today the population limits (e.g. men-only, pregnancy, children) are enforced only inside this gate, so ungating via data would drop those safeguards. Claim-free scoped credit waits for the shared applicability change (no claim / aligned claim / unrelated claim / population mismatch) under /pg-scoring-change.
